surgeons.name: Dr Trent Lincoln
surgeons.roleLine: Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeon, Founder. BMed (Hons), BDSc, FRACDS (OMS)
surgeons.lede: A contemporarily trained oral and maxillofacial surgeon committed to expert care delivered in a compassionate, patient-focused way. Full arch implant rehabilitation is his particular passion, and patients are referred to him from across Queensland for zygomatic and remote anchorage implants.

columns.heading: Beyond the clinic
columns.paragraph: Originally from west of Rockhampton, Dr Lincoln and his wife Alison, a Sunshine Coast local, made the Coast their family's home.

story: After graduating in Medicine with Honours from Monash University, Dr Lincoln returned to Queensland for his residency at the Princess Alexandra Hospital, where treating complex facial trauma led him to oral and maxillofacial surgery. He worked as a registrar in ENT and general surgery in Rockhampton before earning a place in the University of Queensland's lateral-entry Dentistry program, continuing to work in the maxillofacial units of Brisbane's major hospitals while he studied.

He went on to complete the Queensland Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery training program across the Royal Brisbane & Women's, Princess Alexandra, Mater, Queensland Children's, Ipswich and Logan hospitals, with a valuable year in Townsville treating more complex and delayed presentations.

With a strong passion for dental implants and full arch rehabilitation, he undertook advanced training in zygomatic implants in Hong Kong in 2017 and zygomatic, nasal and pterygoid implants in Texas in 2023, then further training with world renowned surgeons from France, Brazil and Spain. He continues to refine his implant, bone and soft tissue grafting skills through global courses and conferences.

surgeons.name: Dr Andrew Higgins
surgeons.roleLine: Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeon, Co-owner. MBBS, BDS, FRACDS (OMS)
surgeons.lede: A fully qualified oral and maxillofacial surgeon with medical and dental degrees and a fellowship of the Royal Australasian College of Dental Surgeons. He practises the full scope of the specialty, with a particular interest in complex implant surgery, grafting, full arch restoration, wisdom teeth and facial trauma.

facts.text: Joined and bought into the practice, now co-owner

columns.heading: Beyond the clinic
columns.paragraph: Andrew surfs, trains and follows rugby league, rugby union and cricket. His wife is also a surgeon on the Sunshine Coast and they have two young boys.

story: Dr Higgins grew up on the Gold Coast and moved to Melbourne to study medicine, graduating in 2008 and working as an intern and surgical resident in Melbourne's tertiary hospitals. Back in Queensland, a surgical senior house officer role in the world-renowned maxillofacial unit at the Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital set his direction, and he became the first lateral entry student in the James Cook University dental program.

His four years of advanced surgical training gave him wide exposure to the full scope of oral and maxillofacial surgery. He passed his fellowship examination in 2019 and received the Robert M Cook Medal for the highest mark in Australia and New Zealand. He attends courses and conferences regularly to stay at the front of surgical technique and is involved in teaching on several courses.
